El. 2,100 → 2,650 ft The climb

Every job here climbs. We plan each level before we frame.

  1. 2,100 ft · River level

    Water repair

    Wet walls opened to the studs, dried, checked with a moisture meter, and only then rebuilt, room by room, at your pace.

  2. 2,350 ft · Mid-slope

    Porches & kitchens

    Sagging bungalow porches rebuilt on new footings, the old stone piers and tapered columns kept. Older kitchens opened up with the view left where it was.

  3. 2,650 ft · Steep ground

    Additions & ADUs

    Footings stepped down the hill, the floor framed dead level, and the drain behind the wall laid before the first stud goes up.

El. 3,250 ft Neighbours

Said by people whose yards slope too.

4.9 from 41 reviews Sample

“Our lot in West Asheville drops eleven feet from the street to the back fence. June's crew stepped the footings down the slope and built a two-bedroom ADU over a walk-out level. My mother lives there now and can see the mountains from her kitchen.”

Sarah M., AshevilleADUs and garage apartments · Sample review

“After the flood our lower level had water up to the outlets. They opened the walls, dried everything, checked it with a moisture meter and only then rebuilt. They never once pushed us to do more than we needed.”

Dennis Y., WoodfinFlood and water damage repair · Sample review

“The porch on our 1918 bungalow was sagging off its piers. They rebuilt it on new footings and reused the old stone, so from the street it looks the same, just level.”

Ruth A., AshevillePorch rebuilds · Sample review

“Our backyard was sliding toward the house every spring. The new wall and drain behind it held through every storm this year and the basement is dry.”
